name: High-rise tailored trousers

lead: High-rise tailored trousers sit at or above the natural waist and are hemmed to a clean length. They raise the visual waistline so the legs take up more of the figure and look longer relative to the torso, an effect that shows straight away in the silhouette.

Proponents say a higher waistband shifts where the eye reads the body's midpoint, and a clean hem keeps the leg line unbroken. Trousers are commonly hemmed to adjust leg length, and no studies of trouser rise and perceived leg length were found.

paras: People choose trousers with a rise at or above the navel, have the hem tailored to the shoe, and tuck tops in to show the waistline. Fit through the seat and thigh and a matching hem length matter to the effect.
Low risk. A high rise can feel restrictive and does not suit every build.

angle.text: High-rise tailored trousers raise the visual waistline so your legs look longer relative to your torso. The change in silhouette is visible straight away; effects on perceived height have not been studied.

lead: High-rise tailored trousers sit at or above the natural waist and are hemmed to a clean length. In height and proportion discussions, proponents say they raise the visual waistline and so make the legs look longer relative to the torso.
Trousers are commonly hemmed to adjust leg length, and higher-quality pairs may leave extra seam allowance at the centre back for adjusting the waist.[1]
No studies of trouser rise and perceived leg length were found in this entry's sources.

paras: Tailors hem trouser legs to prevent fraying and set length, and waists can be adjusted within limits.[1] Rise refers to where the waistband sits; proponents of high rise say a higher waistband shifts the apparent leg-to-torso split upward.
